taffygo_chosen.max_output_tokens: Fireworks publishes no per-model completion cap anywhere read on this date. https://docs.fireworks.ai/guides/querying-text-models states max_tokens 'Default value is 2048 tokens if not specified' and that 'Most models support up to their full context window', and the chat-completions reference states that by default max_tokens is lowered to fit the context window rather than returning an error. Asking for too much is therefore clamped and asking for too little truncates, so the context window is recorded as the cap: it is the only output figure the vendor's own documentation supports, and it is the side of the uncertainty that cannot cut an answer off.
taffygo_chosen.reasoning: The model page's labelled fields cover fine-tuning, serverless, context, function calling, embeddings, rerankers and image input, and say nothing about reasoning. The vendor's own launch post for this model describes 'frontier-level reasoning' in prose and its reasoning guide's example code names Kimi models, so true is TaffyGo's reading of the vendor's prose rather than a labelled capability. thinking_levels is left absent for the same reason, so nothing is invented about how a rung would be spelled.
taffygo_chosen.thinking_levels: Absent, so every rung through HIGH takes the adapter's own default and the two opt-in rungs are unsupported. Fireworks documents reasoning_effort as one generic parameter accepting 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', 'max', 'none' or 'adaptive' and says to 'consult the documentation for your particular model's supported effort levels' — documentation it publishes for no model read on this date. A ladder recorded here would be a set of values nobody published being spelled into a request.
taffygo_chosen.roles: The vendor names no role taxonomy. VISION because the labelled field 'Support image input' reads 'Supported' and 'Function Calling' reads 'Supported', which is what a picture-reading task needs. PRIMARY_REASONING because this is the vendor's largest and dearest serverless model. Not FAST_BROWSING: at $3.00/$15.00 it is twenty times the output price of the other row added for this vendor, and a browsing turn that costs that is a browsing turn nobody would run.
taffygo_chosen.usd_per_million_cache_write: https://docs.fireworks.ai/serverless/pricing publishes three rates per model — input, cached input and output — and names no cache-creation charge anywhere on the page. 0 records that no write charge is published, not a vendor claim that writes are free.

taffygo_chosen.roles: The vendor names no role taxonomy. The model page lists 'Tool Use', 'Browser Search', 'Code Execution', 'JSON Object Mode', 'JSON Schema Mode' and 'Reasoning' as its capabilities, which earns PRIMARY_REASONING, and the same page prints '~500 tps' at $0.15/$0.60, which is fast and cheap enough for FAST_BROWSING as well. No VISION: the page states Text for both input and output.
taffygo_chosen.thinking_levels: https://console.groq.com/docs/reasoning documents reasoning_effort for GPT-OSS 20B and GPT-OSS 120B as exactly 'low', 'medium', 'high', and states that GPT-OSS models do not support reasoning_format. LOW, MEDIUM and HIGH therefore carry the vendor's own literals. OFF: null: the vendor documents a 'none' effort value for the Qwen models on the same page and not for GPT-OSS, so nothing documented turns reasoning off here. MINIMAL: null: not a documented reasoning_effort value. XHIGH: null: not a documented reasoning_effort value. MAX: null: not a documented reasoning_effort value.

provenance.note: Read on 2026-08-29 from https://console.groq.com/docs/model/openai/gpt-oss-120b, which prints context window '131,072', max output tokens '65,536', input '$0.15', cached input '$0.075' and output '$0.60' per million tokens, and '~500 tps'. The vendor's model index at https://console.groq.com/docs/models agrees on all four numbers and lists this model as a production model rather than a preview one. Prompt caching: https://console.groq.com/docs/prompt-caching states 'Prompt caching is provided at no additional cost. There is a 50% discount for cached input tokens.' and lists openai/gpt-oss-20b, openai/gpt-oss-120b and openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b as the models that support it. Cache write is 0 because the vendor states there is no additional fee, not because no rate was found. METERED because the vendor publishes an explicit per-million-token rate on its own model page. Groq publishes no version or effective date beside those rates, so the read date is used as the snapshot label.

taffygo_chosen.usd_per_million_cache_read: Two of the vendor's own pages disagree here and neither is ignorable. The model page prints cached input '$0.037'; the prompt-caching guide states 'There is a 50% discount for cached input tokens', and half of the '$0.075' input rate printed on the same model page is $0.0375. The stated rule is recorded rather than the printed figure, because $0.037 is what $0.0375 looks like rounded to three places — the 120B row on the same vendor prints exactly half its input rate with no rounding to hide — and because under-recording a rate makes every estimate built on it too low.
taffygo_chosen.roles: The vendor names no role taxonomy. FAST_BROWSING only: the model page prints '~1000 tps' at $0.075/$0.30, the fastest and cheapest production model this vendor prices. No VISION: the page states Text for both input and output.

provenance.note: The flagship of the family whose luna and terra rows this catalog already carries. It ships behind the catalog kill switch, and that is the whole point of the row rather than an oversight. Catalog order is the generator's sort by provider then model id, and 'gpt-5.6-sol' sorts before 'gpt-5.6-terra', so an enabled row would take over PRIMARY_REASONING and VISION on this vendor from the model that serves them today and would double what an ordinary reasoning turn costs - 4 against 2 for input, 20 against 12 for output. Which model a person's money is spent on by default is not a change to make by adding a row alphabetically, so the row is complete, priced from the vendor, and switched off until somebody decides. Enabling it is one field.

taffygo_chosen.roles: The vendor names no role. PRIMARY_REASONING because it is the vendor's own flagship, and VISION because its published input modalities include images; it is deliberately not offered for FAST_BROWSING.
taffygo_chosen.thinking_levels: No map is carried, which means every rung through HIGH reaches this model through the adapter's own default rather than through a value quoted from the vendor. The vendor documents no reasoning control for this model, and inventing one here would be a field the provider refuses.
taffygo_chosen.usd_per_million_cache_write: The vendor's caching is automatic and no write charge is published, so writing to cache costs zero rather than a guessed rate.

provenance.note: The bring-your-own candidate for PRIMARY_REASONING on this vendor, at the rate set by the vendor's 2026-07-30 price cut. Cached input is the vendor's published one-tenth of input.

provenance.note: Every figure comes from this vendor's own model page at the address in quoted_from, read on 2026-09-03, at its Singapore (International) rate — the region whose host this provider row names. Function calling, thinking mode, the image input modality, the context window and the maximum output length are all stated there in the vendor's own words. This is the one model of the three whose cache-creation charge the vendor states outright — it publishes an explicit cache creation rate beside the read rate — so usd_per_million_cache_write is the vendor's number rather than an imputed one. The two cache-read readings it gives, an implicit-cache rate and a lower explicit-cache rate, are recorded at the higher of the two as decision 0094 section 2 requires. taffygo_chosen.context_window: The vendor contradicts itself - the docs model table says 524288, the marketing page says 1M. I took the smaller API-table value so a router cannot overrun a real limit.
taffygo_chosen.input_modalities: The vendor also lists Video input; the schema has no VIDEO value, so only TEXT and IMAGE are recorded.
taffygo_chosen.max_output_tokens: Not published by Together; 32768 chosen as a conservative cap.
taffygo_chosen.usd_per_million_cache_write: No cache-write price is published; 0 rather than a guess.
taffygo_chosen.roles: VISION because both the docs vision table and the model page confirm image input; plus FAST_BROWSING because at $0.30/$1.20 with thinking switchable off it is the cheap low-latency multimodal option.
taffygo_chosen.thinking_levels: This model has no graded effort control. The vendor documents a boolean toggle (reasoning={'enabled': true|false}, or chat_template_kwargs {'thinking': false}), so the map carries the JSON literal that field takes at exactly the two rungs that differ: OFF sends false and HIGH sends true. MINIMAL, LOW, MEDIUM, XHIGH and MAX are null rather than repeats of true, because offering a person five rungs that do one thing is a choice this vendor does not give them.

provenance.note: Model page: 'MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3', input modalities 'Text Image Video', 'Function Calling' and 'JSON Mode', a 'toggleable thinking mode' that can be 'enabled for complex reasoning and long-horizon agentic tasks, disabled for fast responses in latency-sensitive scenarios', toggled 'at request time', $0.30 in / $0.06 cached / $1.20 out. Docs table https://docs.together.ai/docs/serverless-models: context 524288, FP4, Function calling Yes, Structured outputs Yes, and its vision table names Minimax M3 as image-capable. taffygo_chosen.context_window: The model page states the context in prose — the model 'scales its context window to 128k tokens in training' and 'aligns its visual encoder with a 128K context length' — with no token figure, so I took the lower decimal reading, 128,000, rather than 131,072. The vendor's own parameter page makes the opposite reading arguable, since it prints a maximum max_tokens of 131072 for the models it calls 128K; the lower figure is recorded because an over-large context claim is a request the provider refuses and the lower one is only a shorter prompt.
taffygo_chosen.thinking_levels: https://docs.z.ai/guides/overview/concept-param documents reasoning_effort for 'GLM-5.2 and above' only, so this model has no effort ladder; what it has is the thinking parameter, whose two documented values are 'enabled' ('Enable chain of thought') and 'disabled' ('Disable chain of thought'). The recorded literals are those two values of thinking.type, not the whole object. OFF maps to the real off value; MINIMAL, LOW, MEDIUM and HIGH all map to the single on value, because one on value is all there is; XHIGH and MAX are null because no third value exists to spell them.
taffygo_chosen.roles: The vendor names no role taxonomy. VISION because the model page states the input modalities as 'Video / Image / Text / File' and says 'GLM-4.6V integrate native Function Calling capabilities for the first time', with 'native multimodal tool calling capability' — a picture-reading role needs both. Not PRIMARY_REASONING or FAST_BROWSING: this is the vendor's vision model, its output allowance is a quarter of the text models' on the vendor's own table, and the two GLM-5 rows added here hold those roles.
taffygo_chosen.usd_per_million_cache_write: The pricing table's four columns are Input, Cached Input, Cached Input Storage and Output; there is no cache-write column at all, and the storage cell for every model reads 'Limited-time Free' with no rate published for when that ends. 0 records what is charged today together with the condition, not a vendor claim that writes are free.
